newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia agency says cuts April palm oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia agency says cuts April palm oil exports.

text.p: Indonesia's Joint Marketing Board (KPB), which markets all crude palm oil produced by state plantations, reduced exports by half in April because of poor production, a senior KPB official said on Friday.

"We reduced exports by 50 percent to 20,000 tonnes in April," the official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters. "The 20,000 tonne shortfall in April was carried over to May, when exports returned to the normal 40,000 tonnes."
"That means 50 percent of the exports in May will be carried over to June, and the same will happen in June through October when we expect the schedule to return to normal," he said.
He said the carry-over of 20,000 tonnes each month until October was necessary because the agency did not want to export 150 percent of the usual amount in any one month.
There was speculation in Malaysia that the agency had cut exports by 50 percent in June, traders said. "It was a factor in the market on Thursday, but not today," one Malaysian trader said.
The KPB official said the agency's allocation of crude palm oil to the local market had not been affected.
He said, however, the agency was reviewing the domestic allocation process but declined to give details.
The official said KPB allocates about 50,000 tonnes of crude palm oil to the domestic market monthly.
